title: Memories That Never Faded
content:
The days continued to pass.

Time never stopped for anyone.

My third-semester examinations slowly came to an end, and only one final exam remained.

Perhaps it was the stress...

Or perhaps it was the loneliness that had once again found its way into my life.

Whatever the reason was, I suddenly found myself thinking about Kiran after a long time.

Without wasting another moment, I called him.

The phone rang only a few times before he answered.

"Hello!"

The moment I heard his voice, it felt as though nothing had changed between us.

He was still the same old Kiran.

We laughed.

We teased each other.

He cracked a few terrible jokes.

I replied with even worse ones.

For a few minutes, it felt like we had gone back to our school days.

But the laughter slowly faded.

There was only one question that had been lingering in my heart.

"Kiran..."

"How's Shreya?"

The moment her name left my lips, the cheerful tone in his voice disappeared.

A heavy silence followed.

Then he asked quietly,

"Why are you asking about her?"

His sudden change in tone made my heart uneasy.

So, I told him everything.

About how Shreya had confessed her love.

About the days we spent talking.

About how she had suddenly begun ignoring me once again.

When I finished, Kiran didn't say a word.

The silence stretched for almost a minute.

"Kiran?" I called.

"What happened?"

"Do you know something?"

He finally spoke.

His voice was calm...

Yet unusually serious.

"I'll tell you only one thing."

"Stop loving her."

"And stop thinking about her."

"For your own sake..."

"Please."

"Just this once..."

"Listen to me."

Before I could ask another question...

The call disconnected.

"Kiran!"

I immediately called him back.

Once.

Twice.

Again and again.

But he never answered.

I slowly lowered my phone.

My heart refused to accept what I had just heard.

Why would Kiran suddenly say something like that?

Did he know something?

Was there something everyone knew except me?

Questions kept flooding my mind.

That entire night...

I couldn't think about anything except Shreya.

Every memory of her returned one after another.

Then...

One particular memory found its way back into my heart.

A memory I had never forgotten.

Our first kiss.

________________________________________

"It happened during our first-semester holidays."

"The day I had to return to college."

"Neither of us wanted to say goodbye."

"So before leaving, I asked her to meet me one last time."

"We met at a small park near her house."

A faint smile appeared on Siddu's face.

"I still remember that evening."

"The setting sun painted the sky with shades of orange."

"A cool breeze gently moved through the trees."

"And there we were..."

"Trying to smile..."

"Even though neither of us wanted the day to end."

"We talked for almost an hour."

"About college."

"About our future."

"About all the things we wanted to do together."

"But as the time to leave came closer..."

"Our smiles slowly disappeared."

Neither of us wanted to say goodbye.

For a few seconds...

We simply looked into each other's eyes.

No words.

Only silence.

A silence that somehow spoke more than words ever could.

Finally, Shreya turned around and began walking away.

But after taking only a few steps...

Her foot slipped.

Without thinking, I rushed forward and caught her before she could fall.

For a brief moment...

She was in my arms.

Neither of us moved.

Our eyes met.

I don't know what we were thinking.

I don't even know who moved first.

Slowly...

Almost unknowingly...

The distance between us disappeared.

Then...

For the very first time...

I felt the gentle touch of her lips against mine.

It was my first kiss.

A moment so simple...

Yet so unforgettable.

Even now...

Years later...

I could still remember every second of it as though it had happened yesterday.

Siddu lowered his eyes.

A faint smile remained on his lips, but there was sadness behind it.

"The more I remembered those days..."

"The more it hurt."

"Every beautiful memory..."

"Only reminded me of how much I had lost."
